sections.html:
To record a Kendall County deed, take it to the County Recorder at 502 S Main St in Yorkville. A single elected office carries both the Clerk and Recorder titles, which is why the county website uses both names. Recording questions go to 630-553-4112.

The building keeps weekday hours of 8:00 to 4:30, yet recording stops sooner: 3:00 p.m. for plats and 4:00 p.m. for all other documents. Show up fifteen minutes late and your deed waits for the next business day. The research area keeps weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Staff give no legal advice and run no document searches, so drafting questions belong with an attorney and title searches with a title company.

A deed costs $76.00 to record under the schedule effective July 1, 2023. Mortgages and most other everyday filings cost the same, while a few special categories run lower or higher.

Kendall County Recorder fee schedule, effective July 1, 2023
DocumentFee
Deed$76.00
Mortgage, assignment, subordination, modification or release$76.00
Easement (not filed by a government body)$76.00
Transfer on death instrument$76.00
Mechanic lien$76.00
Tax lien$57.00
Government or utility filing exempt from the rental housing surcharge$57.00
Re-recording of a document$57.00
Non-standard document$88.00
Plat$110.00 base
Military dischargeNo fee

The price already covers five parcel numbers. Each one past that adds $1.00, which comes up when a sale takes in a house and a neighboring lot. Certified copies start at $27.00 for four pages with $1.00 per extra page, and ordinary photocopies cost $0.50 a page.

Break the layout rules and the deed is billed as non-standard, which adds $12.00 to $76.00 and gives the $88.00 in the table. Watch for these problems:

  • Pages that are not letter size
  • Ink in any color besides black or blue
  • Font below 10 point
  • No blank space in the top right corner of page one for the recording stamp
  • Tape, stickers, labels or greyed areas anywhere on a page

Plan the visit around the cutoffs. A plat that needs three sets of paper and a surveyor's letter takes longer to check at the counter, so bring it early in the day. For a plain deed, make sure every page is letter size and printed in black or blue ink before you leave, since a single bad page moves the whole document to the higher fee.

Plats have their own rules. Subdivision and condominium plats arrive as an original plus two copies with a surveyor's letter of permission, and other plats need an original plus one copy. Each added plat page costs $1.00. The office will not record a plain photocopy of a signed deed. It takes originals and certified copies. A mailed package needs a stamped return envelope addressed to yourself, with a second one if you want copies back.

sections.h2: Paperwork that goes with a deed
sections.html:
A sale deed generally travels with a PTAX-203 transfer declaration, or a signed exemption statement if the transfer qualifies. The recorder's site offers a PTAX-203 exemption list, quit claim and warranty deed forms, a Plat Act affidavit and a redaction request form.

Ask the closing attorney or title company to look over the package first. The counter can reject an incomplete document but cannot draft one. Foreclosure notices take a separate path and go to the Office of the Kendall County Clerk on Main Street in Yorkville.

Recording without a title company? Bring the signed original deed, the completed transfer declaration, payment for the fee and any transfer tax, and the parcel number from your tax bill. Get there well ahead of the 4:00 p.m. cutoff so a small mistake can be corrected that day. Staff will not draft or fix wording for you, so settle any doubts about the deed itself with an attorney before the trip.

The state tax is 50 cents on each $500 of value or fraction of $500, collected by the recorder under 35 ILCS 200/31-15. Paper revenue stamps have been retired, and an electronic stamp or similar marker shows the tax was paid.

Online PTAX-203 filing through MyDec began at the Kendall County Recorder on December 2, 2019, and the Illinois Department of Revenue processes the declaration. Each recorded sale is also reported to the Department electronically. Exemptions are listed in 35 ILCS 200/31-45: a deed with consideration under $100, a tax deed, a deed of partition, or a deed to a mortgage holder after foreclosure, for example. Government or charitable transfers, like-kind exchanges and Home Ownership Made Easy purchases are tax-exempt but still need the declaration.

Before closing, ask the Recorder and the village or city hall where the house stands whether a local stamp or exemption certificate is required.

E-recording is available through the services of CSC and Hopdox, and the Recorder's site also has an online land records search. A title company, lender or attorney holds the vendor account, so a homeowner rarely sets anything up personally.

The office also promotes Property Fraud Alert, a free notice service for recording activity tied to an owner's name. Sign up through the recorder's page. Owners who have just sold or inherited a house can use it to catch an unexpected deed or lien.

Recording and tax billing are separate jobs. The county site gives the Treasurer, the assessment office, the township assessors and the Board of Review their own pages, and the Treasurer's section covers payment, due dates and the annual tax sale.

  • Tax still owed on the parcel: get the balance from the Kendall County Treasurer.
  • A value that looks too high: speak with the township assessor, then the Board of Review.
  • A homestead exemption that is missing: call the assessment office.
  • A new name or mailing address for the bill: contact the Treasurer or Clerk.

A few habits make the closing smoother. Keep the deed, the PTAX-203 and your last tax bill together. Confirm the parcel number on all three matches. If more than one parcel is part of the sale, count them, since parcel numbers past the first five add to the recording fee. After closing, watch for confirmation that the deed was recorded, and use the free fraud alert service if you want notice of any later filing under your name.

Closing agents handle most of this, and the seller mainly supplies the parcel number from the tax bill. In a county of about 145,470 people where owners hold 84.0 percent of homes and the typical owner-occupied value is $322,400, a clean recorded deed history keeps a sale moving.

faqs.q: What is the fee for recording a deed?
faqs.a: The schedule effective July 1, 2023 sets it at $76.00. A non-standard document costs $88.00 instead, and parcel numbers past the first five add $1.00 apiece.

faqs.q: Will the recorder file a copy of my deed?
faqs.a: Only an original or a certified copy will be recorded. Mailed packages need a stamped envelope addressed to you for the return.

faqs.q: What is the daily cutoff at the Recorder?
faqs.a: Recording stops at 4:00 p.m. on weekdays for documents and 3:00 p.m. for plats. The research area runs 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.

faqs.q: Can the PTAX-203 be filed online?
faqs.a: Yes. The Recorder has used MyDec for online PTAX-203 declarations since December 2, 2019, and the form is processed through the Illinois Department of Revenue.

faqs.q: What number do I call about a recording?
faqs.a: Dial the Recorder's office at 630-553-4112. Staff do not give legal advice, so questions about wording go to an attorney.
